text.p: Here highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish Peasants Party (PSL) threatened to call for a no-confidence vote on Poland's Prime Minister if the cabinet does not decide on advance payments for grains harvested in 1997, PSL's board said on Tuesday evening.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- More than 36,000 present and former employees have applied for free shares in the Huta Sendzimira (HTS) steel mill in Krakow, southern Poland, to be privatised this year, HTS said.
- The Komfort Ltd household goods' shopping chain has acquired Belgium's M-3 chain, the companies said.
Komfort is Poland's second biggest retail chain selling floor linings, carpets, floor panels, wallpaper and curtains.
- Poland's second biggest refinery, Rafineria Gdanska, has presented its wholesalers with new fuel price lists showing a 0.02 zloty price rise per litre, the wholesalers said.

- Waiting time for new telephone lines by individual subscribers in the area of Warsaw will be cut to just a few hours following the launch of Motorola's radio access line, the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) state-owned telecoms monopolist said.
- The PTU Energo-Asekuracja insurance firm plans a listing on the Warsaw bourse in 1998, firm deputy president Wieslawa Kwatek said.

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) has contracted 10 banks with outlets in southern Poland to provide low-interest credits to flood victims funded from the state housing fund, BGK said.
- Pekao SA bank has provided a 40 million zlotys credit to the Bydgoszcz municipality in central Poland to buy 60 buses for its urban transport company, the bank said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Austria's Voest Alpine Stahl AG steel holding plans to cooperate with Poland's steel industry to increase its output capacity, holding board member Peter Strahammer said.
The group is not interested in buying into Polish steel plants, Strahammer said.
- Injecting capital into the state-owned PZU SA insurance firm is a condition for the healthy development of Poland's insurance market, Compensa insurer president Krzysztof Lutostanski said.
- Over 34 percent of shoes sold in Poland in the second quarter of 1997 had defects, a report by the PIH state trading standards' authority said.
Shoes imported from China, Korea and Italy proved the most defective.
- The cost of living in Warsaw put it in the thirty seventh position on the list of the world's most expensive cities.

- Adapting the Polish Army to the stadards of NATO will result in an increased number of contracts offered to the Sun Microsystems computer system integrator firm, which provides systems to armed forces across Europe, Sun Sales Manager Jacek Koziaczy said.
Sales of Sun's Polish branch in 1996 reached $20 million, Koziaczy said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank will apply for a loan of 150 million zlotys from the BFG banking guarantee fund to improve its financial results, which will be worse than initially expected as a result of the recent floods, BGZ said.

- Average gross monthly salary in Poland's corporate sector was 1,086 zlotys in the first quarter of 1997, showing a 6.3 percent upturn from the second half of 1996, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland has given a green light to the privatisation of the Pressta missile maker in Bolechow, which will be taken over by its creditor banks in a debt for equity swap.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
